differences: At 600px and below, the movie poster keeps a 92px column while the entire information and management-action stack remains in the adjacent narrow column. The six buttons and keep-up-to-date control therefore read as a long compressed rail instead of a deliberate mobile action area.
The primary Search now action has the same mobile width treatment as secondary maintenance actions, so the main lifecycle action is not clearly prioritized.

The desktop releases and inspector grid starts after the shared Copy and People tools. Moving the inspector beside those tools would require structural markup changes across functional components, so this bounded pass should retain the current desktop order unless a CSS-only change can preserve every control and divider.

Calendar day numbers expose a full-date aria-label directly on a generic span. The visible number should be hidden from assistive technology and paired with explicit screen-reader-only full-date text instead.
planned_changes: At phone widths only, let the hero information wrapper participate in the hero grid so the title and status remain beside the poster while overview, lifecycle notes, downloads, and actions span the full hero width.
Render the phone action area as a compact two-column grid with Search now spanning the full width and all existing buttons, handlers, disabled states, and the keep-up-to-date switch preserved.
Replace the Calendar day-number aria-label with an aria-hidden visible number and screen-reader-only full-date text.
Leave desktop workspace structure unchanged because the requested tightening is not safely achievable as a small CSS-only adjustment.
reasoning: The existing detail workspace is strong on desktop and functionally complete. The remaining high-value polish is a phone-specific composition issue rather than a new component or navigation problem. A responsive grid adjustment can improve hierarchy without changing handlers, permissions, dialogs, or desktop visibility.
